The 3 things they don't want you to know about AI.

Nobody selling you a $2,000 course will say these out loud 🧵👇

1. The free version is enough to start.

You don't need a paid plan, a course or a "prompt pack" to get real work done today. Open it and type.

2. AI is only as smart as what you tell it.

"Write an email" = generic junk.

"I own a bakery. A customer is mad her order was late. Write a kind reply and offer 10% off."

= a reply you'd actually send.

3. You can make AI ask YOU the questions.

Add this to the end of anything:

"Before you answer, ask me 5 questions so you get this right."

Most underrated trick there is.

Bonus: it makes things up sometimes.

Always read before you hit send. It's your assistant, not your boss.

The top AI prompts of 2026 for small business owners.

Copy and paste. Works in Claude or ChatGPT. Save this 🧵👇

1. The reply writer

"Reply to this customer. Friendly, short, answer their question and offer a time to book: [paste message]"

2. The follow up

"Write a 2 sentence follow up for a quote I sent 3 days ago. No pressure, just checking in."

3. The review ask

"Write a short text asking a happy customer for a Google review. Make it sound like me, not a robot."

4. The price defender

"A customer says I'm too expensive. Help me explain my price in a kind, confident way."

5. The day planner

"Here's my to do list. Put it in order of what makes me money first: [paste list]"

6. The bad review fixer

"Help me reply to this bad review calmly and professionally: [paste review]"

7. The caption machine

"Give me 5 short Instagram captions about [what I did today]. Sound human."

8. The secret one

"Ask me 5 questions about my business. Then write instructions so you always answer like my best employee."

That's how you build a Business Brain.

How to use Claude if you've never touched AI.

10 slides. Zero tech words. 🧵👇

1. Go to claude.ai or get the Claude app.

Sign up free with your email. That's the whole setup.

2. Talk to it like texting a smart new employee.

No special words. No "prompt engineering." Just say what you need.

3. Tell it who you are.

"I own a cleaning business in Miami."

One sentence like this changes every answer.

4. Paste stuff in.

Emails, reviews, your menu, even a photo of a receipt. It reads all of it.

5. Don't like the answer? Say so.

"Shorter." "Friendlier." "More like me." It rewrites in seconds.

6. Make it ask you questions first.

"Ask me 3 questions before you answer."

Better questions = better answers.

7. Save your business info once.

Put it in a Project so you never repeat yourself again.

8. Read before you send.

It's fast, not perfect. You're still the boss.
